definition: Police, fire, or a combined public-safety bargaining unit.
Municipal occupations outside police and fire, including clerical, public works, sanitation, parks, libraries, transit, and health roles.
A group of employees represented together for negotiation and contract purposes.
The contract, budget, or pay-setting period to which a compensation action belongs.
A safety and non-safety comparison within the same municipality and compatible compensation cycle.
A process or rule that sets, changes, implements, or constrains pay.
One documented municipal compensation action for a municipality, compensation cycle, compensation mechanism, and side.
Contracts, agreements, awards, ordinances, and reports that document compensation rules or decisions.
A payroll, staffing, budget, pay-plan, schedule, or implementation document.
Collective bargaining agreements, arbitration awards, and factfinding reports that can directly govern compensation terms.
News, commentary, and budget narratives that explain compensation but do not themselves govern a bargaining unit contract.
Evidence with an exact subject, municipality, compatible period, side, pay basis, source identity, and reproducible calculation.
Analytically usable evidence with a stated limitation such as a same-cycle period match or a closely comparable role.
Evidence that identifies a mechanism or direction without supporting a precise magnitude.
Relevant background that does not directly support a claim.
A record excluded because its unit, identity, source support, or direction is incompatible with the proposed use.
A record or result that materially contains both safety and non-safety evidence or both supporting and opposing directions.
A compensation action that applies across municipal roles without a defensible safety or non-safety assignment.
Evidence that cannot be assigned or interpreted reliably with the retained source material.
Evidence with a defensible safety or non-safety assignment.
A map that groups nearby municipalities into equal-sized areas to display regional concentrations of documented events.
The share of an eligible population that has a mechanism or outcome; it requires a valid population denominator.
A change attributable to a mechanism rather than merely observed alongside it.
A difference in wages between two groups measured on a compatible basis and period.
Regular salary or hourly pay before overtime, premiums, allowances, benefits, and one-time payments.
Base wages plus all additional cash compensation and benefits included under a stated definition.
The same general increase applied across covered roles or classifications.
A cost-of-living adjustment, often tied to inflation or a stated index.
Scheduled movement through pay steps based on time, service, qualification, or another stated rule.
A table of pay rates by classification, rank, grade, or step.
A formally adopted structure of classifications, grades, ranges, and compensation rules.
Pay owed for an effective period that began before approval, payroll processing, or payment.
Compensation outside regular base wages, such as overtime, premiums, stipends, and allowances.
Additional pay for a condition, assignment, shift, skill, hazard, or responsibility.
Pay for covered work beyond regular hours under an applicable rate or rule.
Additional compensation based on completed years of service.
A nonrecurring payment that does not permanently raise the base wage unless the source says otherwise.
The practical power employees, unions, or employers can use to influence negotiated terms.
Negotiation between an employer and an employee representative over compensation and working conditions.
A process in which an arbitrator resolves disputed terms of a new or renewed agreement.
A formal review that evaluates an unresolved labor dispute and may recommend settlement terms.
A pay change intended to align a role or schedule with a stated labor market or comparator group.
Hiring, vacancy, retention, workload, or minimum-staffing conditions cited in a compensation decision.
Difficulty attracting or keeping employees that is cited to justify a pay change or premium.
A change to a job classification, grade, band, range, or assigned pay level.
A narrowing pay difference between roles, ranks, grades, or experience levels.
Formal authorization of compensation terms through municipal legislative action.
A stage at which a compensation term is scheduled to operate in payroll; it remains distinct from observed payment.
Retained evidence showing that a payment occurred, rather than only that it was proposed, adopted, or scheduled.
Independent source support that increases confidence without multiplying the underlying event count.
Reviewed evidence that runs against or narrows a proposed generalization.
Evidence kept out of clean calculations because an unresolved conflict could change its meaning or direction.
